fields.description:
## Problem

An async `verify_completion` run whose verdict is FAIL returns `findings: null`
from `gate_status(job_id)`. The caller learns the verdict but never why.
A `review_plan` job instead returns a populated `findings` descriptor pointing at
its `REVIEW_RESULT` sidecar.

Observed this session on `cfe0-4b2b`, and again on `f3b2-6bb8`:

```
{"status": "passed", "gate_type": "verify_completion",
 "verdict": "FAIL", "findings": null}
```

Note `status` is `passed`: `_terminal_from_result` (`src/rebar/_mcp_llm.py:116-122`)
classifies any non-error result as `passed` carrying its own verdict, so a FAIL is
a run that COMPLETED. `status: failed` means the run errored, or was congested.

The `COMPLETION_VERDICT` sidecar carrying the real findings HAD been written and
was readable by hand from the tickets branch. The data was never discarded. It was
never surfaced.

Cost: reading a completion FAIL's reason requires hand-reading the tickets branch,
or a duplicate billable gate pass.

## Scope

One FAIL sub-case stays unreadable by design. On the `LLMError` path
`_verify_completion_body` (`src/rebar/_mcp_llm.py:107-110`) returns
`_structured_llm_failure(exc)` BEFORE `_record_verify_completion`, so
`completion_sidecar.emit` never runs and no sidecar exists. That run records
`status: failed` with an `error`, and its descriptor correctly reports
`readable: false`. This work does not change that path.

## Root cause

1. `src/rebar/llm/gate_runs.py:201-203` — `_review_result_status()` returns `None`
   unless `gate_type == _PLAN_REVIEW`. `gate_run_status()` at
   `src/rebar/llm/gate_runs.py:316-318` sets `out["findings"]` only when that helper
   returns non-None, so the key is absent for every completion run.

2. Neither correlation field reaches a completion index record. `sidecar_emitted` is
   stamped by the CALLER on the plan-review path
   (`src/rebar/llm/plan_review/__init__.py:578`). The completion caller does not:
   `src/rebar/_commands/transition_close.py:189` binds
   `sidecar_written = completion_sidecar.emit(result, ...)` into a local and returns it
   inside a separate `_outcome` dict at
   `src/rebar/_commands/transition_close.py:198-199`, never writing
   `result["sidecar_emitted"]`. `sidecar_reviewed_at` has no completion writer at all:
   `emit()` returns a bare `bool` and discards the timestamp `append_event` returns.

3. No `COMPLETION_VERDICT` timestamp reader exists.
   `_latest_review_result_timestamp` (`src/rebar/llm/gate_runs.py:154-158`) delegates to
   `plan_review.sidecar.latest_review_timestamp`
   (`src/rebar/llm/plan_review/sidecar.py:263`). `completion_sidecar` exposes only
   `latest_fail_verdict`, `latest_pass_record` and `latest_screen_tally`, which return
   verdict dicts, not an `int`.

Timestamp correlation is what makes the descriptor trustworthy: reporting the newest
sidecar without it would attribute a prior run's findings to this job.

## Design

`completion_sidecar.py`. `_append_sidecar_retrying()` returns the timestamp
`append_event` returns. `emit()` stamps BOTH fields on the verdict dict it already
receives as its first parameter: `verdict["sidecar_emitted"]` on every path,
`verdict["sidecar_reviewed_at"]` only on a successful append. Stamping goes inside
`emit()` rather than in its caller — the plan-review placement — because
`transition_close.py:189` keeps the bool in a local that never returns to the verdict.
The mutation is visible to the daemon: `_record_verify_completion`
(`src/rebar/_mcp_llm.py:50-69`) passes that same dict to `record_completion_verdict`
then returns it, and `_spawn_gate_daemon` reads `result` at `src/rebar/_mcp_llm.py:168`.
`emit()` keeps its `bool` return, so no caller changes.

Add `latest_verdict_timestamp(ticket_id, *, repo_root)` to `completion_sidecar`,
mirroring `plan_review/sidecar.py:263`: it reads the ns prefix of
`<ts>-<uuid>-COMPLETION_VERDICT.json` filenames, needs no JSON parse, and returns `None`
on any error.

`_mcp_llm.py`. Rename `_plan_review_sidecar_fields` to `_gate_sidecar_fields` and widen
its guard to admit `verify_completion` alongside `plan_review`. Its body already reads
exactly the two fields now stamped.

`gate_runs.py`. Add `_COMPLETION_VERDICT = "COMPLETION_VERDICT"`. Parameterise
`_latest_review_result_timestamp` by a latest-timestamp reader, and
`_has_review_result_timestamp` by sidecar kind plus accepted schema set.
`_review_result_status` resolves gate type through a module-level mapping — `plan_review`
to `REVIEW_RESULT` with `{plan_review_result_v1, plan_review_result_v2}` and
`latest_review_timestamp`; `verify_completion` to `COMPLETION_VERDICT` with
`{completion_verifier_pass_v1, completion_verifier_fail_v1}` and
`latest_verdict_timestamp` — returning `None` for any other gate type, which preserves
today's behaviour for `code_review`. Its `sidecar_type` output field reports the resolved
kind. The non-terminal early return at `src/rebar/llm/gate_runs.py:214-216`, which yields
`reason` `run-<status>`, is left in place and now applies to both gate types, so a running
completion job reports `run-running`. The mapping is a module-level table, not added
branches, so each touched function stays under its complexity ceiling.

## Verification

Every behavioural criterion below is proven by

```
pytest tests/unit/test_gate_status_sidecar_visibility.py -v
```

which must exit zero with every test passing; each criterion has a named test there.
Repository gates are proven by `make lint`, `make typecheck`,
`python scripts/check_complexity_baseline.py --check`, and
`python scripts/check_mechanism_delta.py --check`, each exiting zero.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] A `verify_completion` job with verdict FAIL returns a non-null `findings` object from `gate_status`.
- [x] That `findings` object reports `sidecar_type` as `COMPLETION_VERDICT`.
- [x] That `findings` object reports `readable` as `true` when a matching sidecar exists.
- [x] A `verify_completion` job with verdict PASS returns a non-null `findings` object.
- [x] `completion_sidecar.emit()` stamps `sidecar_reviewed_at` on the verdict dict on a successful append.
- [x] `completion_sidecar.emit()` leaves `sidecar_reviewed_at` unset when the append fails.
- [x] `completion_sidecar.emit()` stamps `sidecar_emitted` as `true` on a successful append.
- [x] `completion_sidecar.emit()` stamps `sidecar_emitted` as `false` when the append fails.
- [x] `_append_sidecar_retrying` returns the timestamp from `append_event`.
- [x] `completion_sidecar.latest_verdict_timestamp` returns the newest sidecar's filename timestamp.
- [x] `completion_sidecar.latest_verdict_timestamp` returns `None` when the ticket has no sidecar.
- [x] The completion index record carries `sidecar_reviewed_at` after a terminal run.
- [x] The completion index record carries `sidecar_emitted` after a terminal run.
- [x] `_gate_sidecar_fields` returns an empty dict for gate type `code_review`.
- [x] `gate_status` on a `code_review` job omits the `findings` key.
- [x] A `plan_review` job's `findings` object still reports `sidecar_type` as `REVIEW_RESULT`.
- [x] A `plan_review` job's `findings` object still reports `readable` as `true` for a current sidecar.
- [x] A completion sidecar whose timestamp differs from the record's reports `readable` as `false`.
- [x] A completion job in `running` state reports reason `run-running`.
- [x] An `LLMError` completion run reports `readable` as `false`.
- [x] `python scripts/check_complexity_baseline.py --check` reports no new entries.
- [x] `python scripts/check_complexity_baseline.py --check` reports no increased entries.
- [x] `python scripts/check_mechanism_delta.py --check` passes (exit 0) with no **unadmitted** new or increased entries.
      _Corrected from "reports no new entries": the summary's `new=` count includes entries admitted by `mechanism-ok` markers, and the ratchet exits zero only when every new/increased key is admitted (`scripts/check_mechanism_delta.py:27-28`). On the merged tree the count is `new=25`, and **all 25 are admitted** — none of them live in any of this fix's 4 changed files, so the original wording described a pre-existing property of the tree that no change to these files could alter._
